perspective:
Ethan Mohamud’s available information:

- He knows he is Ethan, a plumber, and that Gary Guo is his long-time friend since middle school and works as a doctor.
- He noticed Gary working excessively long hours at the hospital, often skipping meals and sacrificing sleep. He became concerned for Gary’s health.
- Ethan invited Gary to a two-day weekend retreat for relaxation and rejuvenation.
- Gary initially declined, saying he had too much to do at the hospital.
- Ethan was with Gary at the retreat. There he observed Gary acting restless and avoiding discussions about work.
- Ethan suspected something deeper than professional obligations and confronted Gary, telling him they had been friends since middle school, that Gary could tell him anything, and that he was there to help, not judge.
- Gary told Ethan it was complicated and that he hadn’t wanted to burden him. Gary then opened up about pressures from managing a new department and personal challenges.
- Ethan felt relief and empathy, and suggested Gary prioritize tasks and delegate responsibilities. Gary agreed and said he could use help organizing his schedule to make time for himself.
- Over the following months, Ethan regularly checked in with Gary about his progress and challenges. Gary told him things were better, that Ethan’s help made him less overwhelmed, and that he had time for a movie one weekend. Ethan felt hopeful and proud.
- After a year, Ethan saw Gary as capable of managing on his own and believed Gary had reached a healthier balance. He felt satisfied and happy, decided to step back, and told Gary he was always just a call away if needed.
- Gary thanked Ethan, said he couldn’t have done it without his support, and said he felt more in control.
